# Doors: 3D-printed parts

Four door types, all for the same robot drawer. Pick one in the simulator; each has its own printed parts here.

| Door | How it opens | Out while moving | Out when open | Printed parts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Lift door** | 6 mm panel slides up 147 mm behind the drawer front | 0 | 0 | 4 channels, saddle, foot, clamp |
| **Flap out** | Flap swings up and out to 90° | 207 mm | 207 mm | Lever, top mount |
| **Up & over** | Tilts up and slides into the cabinet, above the robot | 35 mm | 13 mm | 2 print-in-place modules, 2 tracks, top mount |
| **Parallel lift** | Moves out, then up, stays vertical | 40 mm | 23 mm | 2 print-in-place modules, top mount |

"Out" = how far the door comes in front of the drawer front. All doors use the same 12 V actuator (150 mm stroke, ≈225 mm pin to pin retracted).

## Print settings (all parts)

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Material | PETG: the cabinet is warm and humid |
| Layers | 0.2 mm, first layer also 0.2 mm. The joint gaps are multiples of 0.2 mm |
| Walls / infill | 4 perimeters, 20 %. The pins and the lever need the walls: do not go below 4 |
| Supports / brim | None. Bridges only under the arms, about 14 mm at most on the lever side |
| Elephant-foot compensation | 0.1–0.2 mm |
| Orientation | As exported |
| Bed | 220 × 220 mm |

**Print-in-place joints (up & over, parallel lift):** print `coupon.stl` first. Twist each test joint firmly once and use
the smallest gap that then turns freely. Joint `P` is the big bore at 0.45 mm: if 45 turns but `P` stays stiff, use 0.55.
If your gap is not 0.45, rebuild with `doors/build.sh -D cj=0.35`: the door wedge (below) follows the gap.
After printing, move each module through its full travel a few times until all joints run smoothly. The lever-side joint has the longest bridge, so expect its first twist to be the stiffest. A joint that sticks:
run a 0.4 mm nozzle-cleaning needle around the gap from the bed side, do not force it.

Slicer tips, these matter most for a joint that comes free: random seam (never "rear": pin and ring seams would face each other),
minimum travel for retraction 0.5 mm so it retracts across the gap, PETG at the low end (about 235 °C), outer wall at most 30 mm/s, fan about 50 %.

## How the hinges work

| Part | Design | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Joint | Hourglass pin in a ring with an inner lip, 0.45 mm gap, all flanks 45° | Thickest at the root, where bending peaks. Calculated about 2.2–2.6 × the load of the old diamond pin with the same outside size, and less free tilt (5.5° instead of 7.7°) |
| Bracket underside | Grows out at 45° from the pins | Replaces a 19 mm bridge over the rings, the print's worst spot |
| Wall plate | Rings + screw bosses + ribs, all full height | The ribs follow the load paths (FE-checked). Prints as solid walls |
| Arms | Front arm 18 → 12 mm wide; rear arm 9.5 mm | The front arm carries actuator or rod torque, the rear arm only pull and push |
| Door flange | Wedged 2.25° | The door's weight takes up all joint play, which would lean its top 8 mm out when closed. The wedge cuts this to about 2 mm and still leaves 2 mm to the drawer front when parked |

Printed filament, 4 perimeters (estimate from the slices, old versions at their 3 perimeters):

| Module pair | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| Parallel lift, left + right | 326 g | 217 g |
| Up & over, left + right | 270 g | 166 g |

**Actuator: rated 50–100 N, with the stall stop set up** (`stall_current` in the ESPHome config, about 0.3 A above the running current).
Calculated pin capacity is about 410–560 N, and a 100 N actuator jammed at one side's door corner puts up to about 400 N on the worst pin, so the stall stop is
what protects the joints (`max_duration` backs it up if the sensor fails). A stronger actuator is not a gain here. The weakest spot in misuse is the door screws:
a 150 N yank on a corner of the open door can pull them out if they work alone (estimated safety factor 0.5–0.75), so **glue the flanges to the door**, see the door steps.
All of this is calculated, not yet broken on the bench.

## Test before you fit the door

No part of this design has been printed yet. These tests decide whether it is sound; stop at the first failure and report it.

| # | Test | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `coupon.stl`: one firm twist on each joint | The 0.45 joint and joint `P` turn freely, no cracks |
| 2 | Spare coupon, 0.45 joint: clamp the base tab in a vice, pull the post sideways with a luggage scale until it breaks | Calculated 410–560 N for the pin. Note where it broke. Under 200 N: do not use the design |
| 3 | Module: free all joints. Screw the plate to a board, hold the plate and rock the bracket by hand | Moves through the full travel, no binding, no cracks |
| 4 | Same module on the board: pull the bracket away from the plate with the scale, along the arms, to 200 N for 10 s. That is the worst pin load with a 50 N actuator stalled at one side | No cracks or whitening, still turns freely |

## Lift door

![Lift door: closed, open, prints](lift_motion.png)

| File | Qty | What |
|---|---|---|
| `lift_channel.stl` | 4 | U-channel, 190 mm. 2 per side, one above the other. Replaces the alu profile |
| `lift_saddle.stl` | 1 | Clip over the panel's top left corner. The actuator rod pushes into its cup |
| `lift_foot.stl` | 1 | Clevis for the actuator's bottom eye, on the tray |
| `lift_clamp.stl` | 1 | Holds the actuator upright on the left cheek (zip tie) |
| `lift-door.scad` | | Source. Customizer: actuator length, rod eye, body diameter |

| Step | What to do |
|---|---|
| 1 | Channels: front edge 2 mm behind the cheek front edge, lower one on the tray, upper one on top of it. A piece of 1.75 mm filament in the end holes lines them up. 3 screws 3.5 × 16 each |
| 2 | Foot: centre 32 mm behind the cheek front edge, 36 mm from the left cheek. 2 screws 4 × 16 |
| 3 | Actuator bottom eye into the foot (M6 bolt + nut). Clamp at 145 mm above the tray, notch over the channel. 2 screws 4 × 16, zip tie round the actuator |
| 4 | Saddle on the panel's top left corner, centre 33 mm from the panel's left edge. M3 × 16 bolt + nut through lip, panel and plate (hidden behind the drawer front) |
| 5 | Panel into the channels. Closed it rests on the tray, the rod tip 3 mm under the cup |

Check (`check_simple.py`): panel rises 147 mm. Saddle 5 mm from the drawer front, 17 mm from the clamp. Parts do not touch.

## Flap out

![Flap: closed, half, open, prints](flap_motion.png)

| File | Qty | What |
|---|---|---|
| `flap_lever.stl` | 1 | Lever on the flap's back, reaches 92 mm above the hinge. Replaces the bent steel L-bracket |
| `flap_mount.stl` | 1 | Actuator top mount on the left cheek, ±8 mm slots |
| `flap.scad` | | Source |

| Step | What to do |
|---|---|
| 1 | Lever on the flap's back: outer face 55 mm from the flap's left edge, lower end 80 mm below the hinge axis. 3 screws 3.5 × 25 |
| 2 | Top mount: bolt 28 mm behind the cheek front edge, 525 mm above the tray. 3 screws 4 × 25 |
| 3 | Actuator: top eye on the mount boss, rod eye on the bay side of the lever pin (M6, washer between) |
| 4 | Retract the actuator fully, slide the mount until the flap just closes, tighten |

Check (`check_simple.py`): stroke 225 → 375 mm, lever arm 60–107 mm, holding force max 21 N.

## Up & over

![Up & over: closed, tilting, nearly open, open](upover_motion.png)

Like a small garage door. A peg on each door bracket runs in a short track; one arm per side tilts the door up.
Open, the door lies flat inside the cabinet, 137 mm above the tray, above the robot.

| File | Qty | What |
|---|---|---|
| `coupon.stl` | 1 | **Print first.** 3 test joints, 0.35 / 0.45 / 0.55 mm gap, plus big joint `P` |
| `upover_left.stl` | 1 | Left module, with the actuator lever. Printed half open, 206 × 206 mm |
| `upover_right.stl` | 1 | Right module, 197 × 134 mm |
| `upover_track_left.stl`, `upover_track_right.stl` | 1 + 1 | Tracks for the pegs |
| `upover_mount.stl` | 1 | Actuator top mount + rod-eye spacer |
| `upover_template.stl` | 1 | Drill template for plate and track screws |
| `up-over.scad` | | Source |

**Door:** 492 × 202 mm (2 mm lower than the other doors: 6 mm gap under the drawer front). No chamfer needed.

![Up & over: print layout](upover_print.png)

| Step | What to do |
|---|---|
| 1 | Template on the cheek: front edge against the back of the front leg, bottom edge on the tray. Pre-drill the 5 plate holes and 3 track holes (3 mm). Left cheek: turn it over like a page |
| 2 | Modules on the cheeks: 5 screws 4 × 20 each, from the robot side |
| 3 | Tracks over the pegs (slot towards the bay), 3 screws 3 × 16 each. A little grease in the slot |
| 4 | Door: hold it in place, closed. Brackets: bottom edge 23 mm above the door's bottom edge. Polyurethane or epoxy glue on the flange face (sand the PETG first), 3 screws 3.5 × 16 per bracket at 45° from the bay side (pre-drill 2.5 mm through the bracket holes) |
| 5 | Top mount: bolt 13 mm behind the cheek front edge, 428 mm above the tray. 3 screws 4 × 25 |
| 6 | Actuator: rod eye with the printed spacer on the lever (nyloc nut in the hex pocket), top eye on the mount boss |
| 7 | Retract fully, slide the mount until the door is just shut, tighten |

No sync rod: the arms sit at 98 mm height, right over the robot. The door itself keeps both sides in step.

Check (`check_upover.py`): joint gap 0.45 mm, other moving gaps ≥ 1.0 mm, each body one piece. Door ≥ 2.5 mm from the drawer front and from
the docked robot, 2 mm above the tray. Actuator 225 → 375 mm, no dead point, holding force max 39 N.
The peg is now Ø10 mm and its slot runs 3 mm past the open position, so the peg never ends up against the slot's end.

## Parallel lift

![Parallel lift: closed, half way, open](parallel_motion.png)

The door stays vertical. It moves out, then up on a circle and parks 116 mm higher, only 3.5 mm in front of the drawer front.

| File | Qty | What |
|---|---|---|
| `coupon.stl` | 1 | **Print first.** 3 test joints plus big joint `P` |
| `parallel_left.stl` | 1 | Left module, with the actuator lever. Printed open, 168 × 212 mm |
| `parallel_right.stl` | 1 | Right module, 144 × 212 mm |
| `parallel_mount.stl` | 1 | Actuator top mount + rod-eye spacer |
| `parallel_template.stl` | 1 | Drill template for the plate screws |
| `parallel-lift.scad` | | Source |

**Door:** 492 × 204 mm. **45° chamfer on the top back edge, leave a 1 mm flat at the front.** It lets the door slide past
the drawer front's bottom edge; from the front you do not see it.

![Parallel lift: print layout](parallel_print.png)

| Step | What to do |
|---|---|
| 1 | Template on the cheek (front edge on the back of the front leg, bottom edge on the tray). Pre-drill the 5 holes. Left cheek: turn it over |
| 2 | Left module on, 5 screws 4 × 20 from the robot side |
| 3 | Solid steel square rod 8 × 8 mm into the square hole of the left front arm, 14 mm deep (tight on purpose: file the hole if the rod does not go in). Length = distance between the cheeks − 16 mm (502 → 486 mm) |
| 4 | Right module onto the other end of the rod, then screw it on |
| 5 | Door: hold it closed. Bracket bottom = door bottom edge, outer face = door side edge. Pull the door flat against the flange: the flange is wedged on purpose (see "How the hinges work"), so do not shim it. Polyurethane or epoxy glue on the whole flange face (sand the PETG first), 3 screws 3.5 × 16 per bracket at 45° from the bay side (pre-drill 2.5 mm) |
| 6 | Top mount: bolt 59 mm behind the cheek front edge, 455 mm above the tray. Actuator with the spacer on the lever, as above |
| 7 | Retract fully, slide the mount until the door is flush, tighten |

Check (`check_parallel.py`): joint gap 0.45 mm, other gaps ≥ 1.0 mm, each body one piece. With the door's weight on the joints: top about 2 mm out when closed, 2 mm from the drawer front parked (1.3 mm if your real gap
comes out 0.1 mm tighter than set), 2 mm above the tray. Actuator 225 → 375 mm, holding force max 14 N.

## Reeds (all doors)

| Reed | Where |
|---|---|
| Door closed | Lift: on the tray under the panel. Others: magnet on the back of a bracket's (or the lever's) lower end, reed right behind it |
| Door open | Magnet on the lever tip (lift: on the saddle), reed where it stops. Set it so the door stops before the actuator's own end stop |

ESPHome: no change. Same endstop cover with both reeds.

## Hardware for every door

| Part | Qty |
|---|---|
| Linear actuator 12 V, 150 mm stroke, 50–100 N (see "How the hinges work"), ≈225 mm pin to pin retracted | 1 |
| M6 bolts (eye thickness + 25 mm), nyloc nuts, washers | 2 |
| Countersunk wood screws, see the steps | – |

## Rebuild + check

| Command | What |
|---|---|
| `doors/build.sh` | All STL + `robo-garage-doors_v<version>.zip`. Extra args go to OpenSCAD, e.g. `-D cj=0.35` |
| `python3 doors/check_parallel.py` | Parallel lift: whole travel in 1 % steps (`--quick`: 5 %) |
| `python3 doors/check_upover.py` | Up & over |
| `python3 doors/check_simple.py` | Lift door + flap |
| `python3 doors/render.py` | The pictures in this file |

Needs `openscad`, `zip`, `xvfb-run`; Python `trimesh`, `rtree`, `shapely`, `numpy`, `Pillow`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PNG previews for the README (OpenSCAD + xvfb-run + Pillow). Usage: python3 render.py <type>  (parallel | lift | flap | upover | all)"""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
TMP = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='doorpng_')
FONT = ImageFont.truetype('/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf', 22)

def png(scad, part, defs=(), camera='0,0,0,55,0,25,500', size=(900, 900), name=None, ortho=True, render=False):
    fn = os.path.join(TMP, (name or part) + '.png')
    cmd = ['xvfb-run', '-a', 'openscad', '-q', '--render' if render else '', '--colorscheme=Tomorrow', f'--imgsize={size[0]},{size[1]}',
           f'--camera={camera}', '--viewall' if camera is None else '', '-D', f'part="{part}"']
    cmd = [c for c in cmd if c]
    if ortho: cmd.append('--projection=o')
    for d in defs: cmd += ['-D', d]
    cmd += ['-o', fn, os.path.join(HERE, scad)]
    subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    return Image.open(fn).convert('RGB')

def row(imgs, labels, out, pad=10, bg=(248, 248, 248)):
    h = max(i.height for i in imgs) + 36; w = sum(i.width for i in imgs) + pad * (len(imgs) - 1)
    canvas = Image.new('RGB', (w, h), (255, 255, 255)); x = 0; dr = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)
    for im, lab in zip(imgs, labels):
        canvas.paste(im, (x, 36)); dr.text((x + 12, 6), lab, fill=(20, 20, 20), font=FONT); x += im.width + pad
    canvas.save(os.path.join(HERE, out), optimize=True); print(out, canvas.size)

def top_view(cx, cy, dist=800):      # looking from the cheek side (+Z) at the X-Y plane
    return f'{cx},{cy},{dist},{cx},{cy},0'

def parallel():
    poses = [(0, 'closed'), (0.5, 'half way: 40 mm out (max)'), (1, 'open: 23 mm out, 116 mm up')]
    imgs = [png('parallel-lift.scad', 'scene', [f'pose={p}'], top_view(95, 262, 1500), (520, 800), name=f'pl_{i}') for i, (p, _) in enumerate(poses)]
    row(imgs, [l for _, l in poses], 'parallel_motion.png')
    lay = png('parallel-lift.scad', 'layout', [], '225,110,0,0,0,0,800', (1100, 560), name='pl_layout', ortho=True)
    lay.save(os.path.join(HERE, 'parallel_print.png'), optimize=True); print('parallel_print.png', lay.size)

def upover():
    poses = [(0, 'closed'), (0.35, 'tilting: 35 mm out (max)'), (0.7, 'nearly open'), (1, 'open: inside, 13 mm out')]
    imgs = [png('up-over.scad', 'scene', [f'pose={p}'], top_view(95, 262, 1500), (440, 800), name=f'uo_{i}') for i, (p, _) in enumerate(poses)]
    row(imgs, [l for _, l in poses], 'upover_motion.png')
    lay = png('up-over.scad', 'layout', [], '225,110,0,0,0,0,800', (1100, 560), name='uo_layout', ortho=True)
    lay.save(os.path.join(HERE, 'upover_print.png'), optimize=True); print('upover_print.png', lay.size)

def lift():
    imgs = [png('lift-door.scad', 'scene', [f'pose={p}'], top_view(60, 230, 1300), (440, 760), name=f'ld_{i}') for i, p in enumerate((0, 1))]
    s = png('lift-door.scad', 'set', [], '100,110,30,55,0,25,520', (700, 760), name='ld_set', ortho=False)
    row(imgs + [s], ['closed', 'open: 150 mm up', 'prints (one bed)'], 'lift_motion.png')

def flap():
    imgs = [png('flap.scad', 'scene', [f'pose={p}'], top_view(-20, 320, 1500), (520, 760), name=f'fl_{i}') for i, p in enumerate((0, 0.5, 1))]
    s = png('flap.scad', 'set', [], '70,100,10,55,0,25,420', (600, 760), name='fl_set', ortho=False)
    row(imgs + [s], ['closed', 'half', 'open 90°', 'prints'], 'flap_motion.png')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    what = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'all'
    for k, fn in [('parallel', parallel), ('upover', upover), ('lift', lift), ('flap', flap)]:
        if what in (k, 'all'): fn()

#!/bin/bash
# Printed door parts: STL per print (OpenSCAD) -> release zip. Extra args go to OpenSCAD, e.g. ./build.sh -D cj=0.35
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
V=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' parallel-lift.scad)
[ -n "$V" ] || { echo "version not found in parallel-lift.scad"; exit 1; }
stl() {   # OpenSCAD keeps going on errors and silently drops the broken geometry: fail the build instead
  local log; log=$(openscad --export-format binstl -D "part=\"$2\"" "${@:4}" -o "$3" "$1" 2>&1)
  if grep -qE '^ERROR|undefined' <<<"$log"; then echo "$3: $(grep -E '^ERROR|undefined' <<<"$log" | head -3)" >&2; touch "$3.failed"; fi
}
for p in left right mount template; do stl parallel-lift.scad "$p" "parallel_$p.stl" "$@" & done
for p in left right mount template; do stl up-over.scad "$p" "upover_$p.stl" "$@" & done
wait
stl up-over.scad track upover_track_right.stl "$@" &
stl up-over.scad track_l upover_track_left.stl "$@" &
stl parallel-lift.scad coupon coupon.stl "$@" &
for p in channel saddle foot clamp; do stl lift-door.scad "$p" "lift_$p.stl" "$@" & done
for p in lever mount; do stl flap.scad "$p" "flap_$p.stl" "$@" & done
wait
if ls ./*.failed >/dev/null 2>&1; then rm -f ./*.failed; echo "OpenSCAD errors, see above"; exit 1; fi
rm -f robo-garage-doors_v*.zip parallel_coupon.stl upover_coupon.stl upover_track.stl
zip -q -X "robo-garage-doors_v$V.zip" README.md ./*.scad ./*.py build.sh ./*.stl ./*.png
echo "doors/robo-garage-doors_v$V.zip"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check the print-in-place parallel lift (parallel-lift.scad).

Renders every body with OpenSCAD, slices it every 0.2 mm and moves the slices through the whole door travel
(f = 0 closed .. 1 open, 1 % steps). Reports per pair of parts the smallest gap in the joints and elsewhere,
the door path against the drawer front, the cabinet obstacles, the actuator, screw access, print overhangs and
the bed footprint at the print pose.
Usage: python3 check_parallel.py [--quick] [cj=0.45] [cs=1.0] [gz=0.6]
"""
import math, os, sys
import numpy as np
from shapely.geometry import Polygon, Point, LineString, box
from shapely.ops import unary_union
from shapely import affinity
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from checklib import HERE, defs_from_argv, scad_echo, render, slices, layer_zs, overhangs, screw_walls, footprint, fmt_gap

SCAD = os.path.join(HERE, 'parallel-lift.scad')
QUICK = '--quick' in sys.argv
DEFS = defs_from_argv()
G = scad_echo(SCAD, DEFS)
P1, P2, A1, A2, F = (np.array(G[k], float) for k in ('P1', 'P2', 'A1', 'A2', 'F'))
R, TH0, SW, LEV, LEV_A = (float(G[k]) for k in ('R', 'TH0', 'SWING', 'LEV', 'LEV_A'))
CJ, CS, GZ, Z_TOP, Z_MOV = (float(G[k]) for k in ('cj', 'cs', 'gz', 'z_top', 'z_mov'))
d = lambda a: np.array([math.cos(math.radians(a)), math.sin(math.radians(a))])
T = lambda f: R * (d(TH0 - SW * f) - d(TH0))
C = lambda f: P1 + LEV * d(LEV_A - SW * f)

DOOR = affinity.translate(Polygon([(-19, 17), (0, 17), (0, 203), (-18, 221), (-19, 221)]), 0, G['door_up'])   # door section, 45 deg back chamfer, 1 mm flat
VEDD = box(-19, 225, -3, 700)                                                # drawer front (VEDDINGE)
WHEEL = box(55, 0, 85, 30)                                                   # drawer wheel, Z 9..19 in the module frame
Z_ACT = -(G['act_gap'] + 4)                                                  # actuator plane: spacer + half an 8 mm eye


def door_loaded(f, g):
    """Door pose with the joint play of radial gap g taken up by its weight: (polygon, lean in deg, + = top outwards). Both sides averaged:
    the door is stiff. Each pin sits g off its ring centre, against the force. The rear arm only pushes; the front arm also carries shear."""
    u, t = d(TH0 - SW * f), T(f)
    a1, a2, cg = A1 + t, A2 + t, np.array([-9.5, 119.0]) + t
    w = np.array([0, -0.5 * 1.48 * 9.81])
    cr = lambda a, b: a[0] * b[1] - a[1] * b[0]
    un = lambda v: v / np.linalg.norm(v)
    sa = -cr(cg - a1, w) / cr(a2 - a1, u)                    # force on the bracket from the rear arm = sa * u
    f1 = -w - sa * u                                         # ... and from the front arm
    pose = []
    for lev in (True, False):
        gg = f1
        if lev:                                              # left front arm: the actuator holds both sides via the rod
            c = C(f); ua = un(F - c)
            gg = f1 - (-2 * cr(a1 - P1, -f1) / cr(c - P1, ua)) * ua
        p1 = P1 - g * un(gg) + R * u - g * un(f1)            # bracket pin A1
        r2 = R - 2 * g * np.sign(sa)                         # rear arm: effective length
        dv = P2 - p1; dd = np.linalg.norm(dv)                # bracket pin A2: BASE from A1, r2 from P2
        aa = (G['BASE'] ** 2 - r2 ** 2 + dd ** 2) / (2 * dd); hh = math.sqrt(max(G['BASE'] ** 2 - aa ** 2, 0))
        e = dv / dd; n = np.array([-e[1], e[0]])
        p2 = min((p1 + aa * e + hh * n, p1 + aa * e - hh * n), key=lambda q: np.linalg.norm(q - a2))
        pose.append((math.degrees(math.atan2((p1 - p2)[1], (p1 - p2)[0])) - G['BDIR'], (p1 + p2) / 2))
    a = (pose[0][0] + pose[1][0]) / 2 - float(G['lean'])
    mid, nom = (pose[0][1] + pose[1][1]) / 2, (A1 + A2) / 2
    # the door lies on the wedged flange: its bottom back corner on the flange's bottom corner, then door + bracket turn together
    y0 = 17 + G['door_up']; lean = float(G['lean'])
    door = affinity.rotate(affinity.translate(DOOR, 0, 0), -lean, origin=(0, y0))
    door = affinity.translate(door, math.tan(math.radians(lean)) * (y0 - G['y_mid']), 0)
    return affinity.translate(affinity.rotate(door, a + lean, origin=tuple(nom)), *(mid - nom)), a


def place(g, kind, f, pivot=None):
    if kind == 'fix': return g
    if kind == 'rot': return affinity.rotate(g, -SW * f, origin=tuple(pivot))
    t = T(f); return affinity.translate(g, t[0], t[1])


def main():
    layers, zs = layer_zs(Z_TOP, [5.95, 6.05, 6.3, 6.55, 6.65])
    fs = np.linspace(0, 1, 21 if QUICK else 101)
    report, ok = [], True
    def fail(msg):
        nonlocal ok; report.append(msg); ok = False

    # ---- door path (2D) ----
    dv = min(affinity.translate(DOOR, *T(f)).distance(VEDD) for f in np.linspace(0, 1, 401))
    outs = [-T(f)[0] for f in np.linspace(0, 1, 401)]
    t1 = T(1)
    print(f'--- door, all joints centred: out max {max(outs):.1f} mm, parked {-t1[0]:.1f} mm out / {t1[1]:.1f} mm up '
          f'(bottom edge {17 + t1[1]:.0f} mm above the floor), gap to the drawer front: min {dv:.1f}, parked {-t1[0] - 19:.1f} mm')
    # no limit here: with its weight on the joints the door never sits like this; the loaded case below is the real test
    if min(T(f)[1] for f in fs) < -0.5: fail('door goes down when opening')
    if max(T(f)[0] for f in fs) > 0.01: fail('door moves into the cabinet')

    # ---- door under gravity: its weight takes up all joint play, which tilts the bracket. Solved from the joint forces, as the
    # front arm's load turns from axial to mostly shear over the travel. Real gaps vary, so test the set gap and 0.1 mm either side.
    print(f'--- door with joint play taken up by its weight (flange wedge {G["lean"]:.2f} deg):')
    for g in (CJ - 0.1, CJ, CJ + 0.1):
        res = [door_loaded(f, g) for f in np.linspace(0, 1, 201)]
        worst = min(dr.distance(VEDD) for dr, _ in res)
        tray = min(dr.bounds[1] for dr, _ in res) - 15
        a0, a1 = res[0][1], res[-1][1]
        print(f'    gap {g:.2f}: lean closed {a0:+.2f}, parked {a1:+.2f} deg; door top {math.radians(a0) * (221 - G["y_mid"]):.1f} mm out when closed; '
              f'gap to the drawer front {worst:.1f} mm (parked {res[-1][0].distance(VEDD):.1f}), to the tray {tray:.1f} mm')
        if worst < 1.0: fail(f'door within {worst:.1f} mm of the drawer front at joint gap {g:.2f}')
        if tray < 1.0: fail(f'door within {tray:.1f} mm of the tray at joint gap {g:.2f}')

    n = len(render(SCAD, 'coupon', DEFS).split(only_watertight=False))
    print(f'--- coupon: {n} separate bodies, 2 per joint')
    if n != 8: fail(f'coupon has {n} bodies, not 8: a joint is fused')

    for side in ('left', 'right'):
        lev = side == 'left'
        bodies = {'plate': ('plate_l' if lev else 'plate_r', 'fix', None),
                  'arm1': ('arm1_l' if lev else 'arm1_r', 'rot', P1),
                  'arm2': ('arm2', 'rot', P2),
                  'bracket': ('bracket', 'move', None)}
        meshes, sl = {}, {}
        for k, (p, kind, piv) in bodies.items():
            m = render(SCAD, p, DEFS); meshes[k] = m
            if not m.is_watertight: fail(f'{side} {k}: mesh not watertight')
            if len(m.split(only_watertight=False)) != 1: fail(f'{side} {k}: not one connected body')
            sl[k] = slices(m, zs)
        print(f'--- {side} module ---')
        for k, m in meshes.items():
            lo, hi = m.bounds
            print(f'  {k:8s} volume {m.volume / 1000:6.1f} cm3  X {lo[0]:6.1f}..{hi[0]:6.1f}  Y {lo[1]:6.1f}..{hi[1]:6.1f}  Z {lo[2]:4.1f}..{hi[2]:4.1f}')
        for k in ('arm1', 'arm2', 'bracket'):
            if meshes[k].bounds[1][2] > Z_MOV + 1e-3: fail(f'{side} {k}: above Z {Z_MOV} (door edge)')
        if meshes['plate'].bounds[1][2] > Z_TOP + 1e-3: fail(f'{side} plate thicker than {Z_TOP}')

        pairs = [('plate', 'arm1'), ('plate', 'arm2'), ('plate', 'bracket'), ('arm1', 'arm2'), ('arm1', 'bracket'), ('arm2', 'bracket')]
        best = {pr: [(1e9, None), (1e9, None)] for pr in pairs}     # [joint zone, elsewhere]
        env = {'tray': 1e9, 'wheel': 1e9, 'drawer front': 1e9, 'door (arms)': 1e9}
        for f in fs:
            placed = {k: {z: place(sl[k][z], bodies[k][1], f, bodies[k][2]) for z in zs} for k in bodies}
            t = T(f)
            jc = {('plate', 'arm1'): (P1, G['rRP1']), ('plate', 'arm2'): (P2, G['rRP2']),
                  ('arm1', 'bracket'): (A1 + t, G['rRA']), ('arm2', 'bracket'): (A2 + t, G['rRA'])}
            door = affinity.translate(DOOR, t[0], t[1])
            for z in zs:
                for a, b in pairs:
                    ga, gb = placed[a][z], placed[b][z]
                    if ga.is_empty or gb.is_empty: continue
                    if (a, b) in jc:
                        c, rz = jc[(a, b)]
                        zone = Point(*c).buffer(rz + 0.6)
                        ia, ib = ga.intersection(zone), gb.intersection(zone)
                        if not ia.is_empty and not ib.is_empty:
                            dd = ia.distance(ib)
                            if dd < best[(a, b)][0][0]: best[(a, b)][0] = (dd, (round(float(f), 2), z))
                        oa, ob = ga.difference(zone), gb.difference(zone)
                        if not oa.is_empty and not ob.is_empty:
                            dd = oa.distance(ob)
                            if dd < best[(a, b)][1][0]: best[(a, b)][1] = (dd, (round(float(f), 2), z))
                    else:
                        dd = ga.distance(gb)
                        if dd < best[(a, b)][1][0]: best[(a, b)][1] = (dd, (round(float(f), 2), z))
                for k in ('arm1', 'arm2', 'bracket'):
                    g = placed[k][z]
                    if g.is_empty: continue
                    env['tray'] = min(env['tray'], g.bounds[1] - 15)
                    if 9 <= z <= 19: env['wheel'] = min(env['wheel'], g.distance(WHEEL))
                    env['drawer front'] = min(env['drawer front'], g.distance(VEDD))
                    if k != 'bracket': env['door (arms)'] = min(env['door (arms)'], g.distance(door))
        pg = unary_union([sl['plate'][z] for z in zs])
        env['plate behind door'] = pg.bounds[0]
        env['plate above tray'] = pg.bounds[1] - 15
        print('  gaps (mm)           joint  where (f, Z)        elsewhere  where (f, Z)')
        for pr in pairs:
            (dj, wj), (de, we) = best[pr]
            js = f'{fmt_gap(dj)}  {str(wj):18s}' if dj < 1e8 else '     -' + ' ' * 20
            print(f'  {pr[0]:8s}-{pr[1]:8s} {js} {fmt_gap(de)}   {we}')
            if dj < 1e8 and dj < CJ - 0.06: fail(f'{side} {pr}: joint gap {dj:.2f} < {CJ}')
            if de < CS - 0.06: fail(f'{side} {pr}: gap {de:.2f} < {CS} at {we}')
        print('  obstacles (mm):', ', '.join(f'{k} {v:.1f}' for k, v in env.items()))
        lim = {'tray': 1.5, 'wheel': 2, 'drawer front': 2, 'door (arms)': 1, 'plate behind door': 1.9, 'plate above tray': 0.4}
        for k, v in env.items():
            if v < lim[k]: fail(f'{side}: {k} margin {v:.1f}')

        # wall plate screws: >= 1.5 mm plastic around the counterbore over its full depth
        rcb = (2 * G['wall_screw'] + 0.6) / 2
        for s, worst in screw_walls(sl['plate'], G['SCREWS'], rcb, Z_TOP - 7.5):
            if worst > 0.5: fail(f'{side} wall screw {s} too close to an edge ({worst:.1f} mm2 missing)')
        print(f'  wall screws {G["SCREWS"]}: walls ok' if all(w <= 0.5 for _, w in screw_walls(sl['plate'], G['SCREWS'], rcb, Z_TOP - 7.5)) else '  wall screws: see problems')

        # door screws: driver from the robot bay at 45 deg must reach the head at every door position
        a = math.radians(G['dsb']); u_out = np.array([math.cos(a), -math.sin(a)])      # (X, Z) from the door towards the head
        sh = G['dze'] / math.sin(a) - 1
        worst = 1e9
        for ys in G['YSC']:
            for f in fs[::5]:
                t = T(f)
                for k in ('plate', 'arm1', 'arm2'):
                    for z in zs:
                        if z > 8: continue
                        g = place(sl[k][z], bodies[k][1], f, bodies[k][2])
                        if g.is_empty: continue
                        reg = []
                        for tt in np.linspace(0, 14, 15):
                            cx, cz = np.array([math.tan(math.radians(G['lean'])) * (ys - G['y_mid']), G['dze']]) + (sh + tt) * u_out
                            dz = z - cz
                            if abs(dz) < 4.2: reg.append(Point(cx + t[0], ys + t[1]).buffer(math.sqrt(4.2 ** 2 - dz ** 2)))
                        if reg: worst = min(worst, g.distance(unary_union(reg)))
        print(f'  door screws at Y {G["YSC"]}: driver path free by {worst:.1f} mm at every door position')
        if worst < 0.5: fail(f'{side}: door screw driver path blocked ({worst:.1f} mm)')

        # actuator (left): tube and body next to the module, in the plane Z_ACT
        if lev:
            worst_a = 1e9
            for f in fs:
                c = C(f); u = (c - F) / np.linalg.norm(c - F)
                parts = [(c - G['act_tube_from'] * u, F + G['act_body_len'] * u, G['act_r_tube']),
                         (F + 15 * u, F + G['act_body_len'] * u, G['act_r_body'])]
                for k in bodies:
                    for z in zs:
                        g = place(sl[k][z], bodies[k][1], f, bodies[k][2])
                        if g.is_empty: continue
                        for p0, p1, r in parts:
                            dz = abs(z - Z_ACT)
                            if dz >= r: continue
                            w = math.sqrt(r * r - dz * dz)
                            worst_a = min(worst_a, g.distance(LineString([tuple(p0), tuple(p1)]).buffer(w, cap_style=2)))
            print(f'  actuator (eye plane Z {Z_ACT:.0f}): clear of the module by {"> 5" if worst_a > 5 else f"{worst_a:.1f}"} mm')
            if worst_a < 1: fail(f'actuator touches the module ({worst_a:.1f} mm)')

        # print pose footprint + overhangs
        fp = print_pose_footprint(sl, bodies, zs)
        print(f'  print footprint (printed open) {fp[0]:.0f} x {fp[1]:.0f} mm, height {Z_TOP:.0f} mm')
        if max(fp) > 218: fail(f'{side}: does not fit a 220 x 220 bed ({fp[0]:.0f} x {fp[1]:.0f})')
        print('  unsupported area per body (outside 45 deg, > 1 mm2):')
        for k in bodies:
            items = overhangs(sl[k], layers)
            print(f'    {k:8s} ' + ('; '.join(f'Z{z:.1f}: {a:.0f} mm2 (widest ~{w:.1f} mm)' for z, a, w in items) if items else 'none'))

    # actuator stroke and holding force (door 1.43 kg + brackets, both sides via the rod)
    l0, l1 = np.linalg.norm(F - C(0)), np.linalg.norm(F - C(1))
    print(f'--- actuator: pin to pin {l0:.1f} mm closed, {l1:.1f} mm open, stroke {l1 - l0:.1f} mm, top pivot X {F[0]:.0f} Y {F[1]:.0f}')
    W, fmax, fcl = 1.48 * 9.81, 0, None
    for f in np.linspace(0, 1, 201):
        a_out = math.radians(180 - (TH0 - SW * f))
        torque = W * R / 1000 * math.cos(a_out)          # N m about the pivots (lift rate dY/dphi = R cos)
        c = C(f); u = (F - c) / np.linalg.norm(F - c); r = (c - P1) / 1000
        arm = abs(r[0] * u[1] - r[1] * u[0]); fa = torque / arm if arm > 1e-6 else 0
        fmax = max(fmax, fa); fcl = fa if fcl is None else fcl
    print(f'--- actuator force to hold the door (no friction): max {fmax:.0f} N, closed {fcl:.0f} N')
    if abs(l1 - l0 - 150) > 1: fail(f'stroke {l1 - l0:.1f} mm, not 150')
    print('RESULT:', 'OK' if ok else 'PROBLEMS\n  ' + '\n  '.join(report))
    return 0 if ok else 1


def print_pose_footprint(sl, bodies, zs):
    f = float(G['print_pose'])
    return footprint([place(sl[k][z], bodies[k][1], f, bodies[k][2]) for k in bodies for z in zs])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
